blocks.explanation: Yeh sawal polar coordinates ka hai: humein ek point graph par lagana (plot karna) hai. Dekhiye, polar point \((r, \theta)\) do baatein batata hai: kis taraf jaana hai (angle \(\theta\)) aur kitni door jaana hai (\(|r|\)). Bilkul aise jaise koi aap ko rasta bataye: "is taraf mudo aur itne qadam chalo". Is part mein r positive hai, is liye angle wali ray par seedha aage chalna hai. Plan yeh hai: angle samjhein, r ka sign dekhein, phir x aur y nikaal kar point bilkul theek jagah lagayein aur aakhir mein faasla check karein.
steps:
Given (diya gaya hai): polar point \((2,\ 75^{\circ})\), yani \(r = 2\) aur \(\theta = 75^{\circ}\).
To find (maloom karna hai): yeh point polar plane par kahan aata hai, aur use plot karna.
Method (tareeqa): pehle polar axis (yani positive x-axis) se angle \(\theta\) jitna ghoomein: \(\theta\) positive ho to anticlockwise (ghari ki suiyon ke ulat), negative ho to clockwise (ghari ki suiyon ki taraf). Phir us ray (seedhi lakeer jo O se shuru ho kar ek taraf jaati hai) par \(|r|\) units chalein. Agar \(r\) negative ho to isi ray ki bajaye ulti (opposite) ray par chalein.

r ka sign dekhein
\(r = 2 > 0\), is liye point isi \(75^{\circ}\) wali ray par hoga.
Kyun: positive r ka matlab hai ray ke saath aage ki taraf chalna. Angle pehle hi degrees mein hai, aur \(75^{\circ}\) first quadrant mein hai (\(0^{\circ}\) aur \(90^{\circ}\) ke darmiyan), is liye point upar-daayein taraf aayega, y-axis ke kaafi qareeb.

Rectangular coordinates nikaalein (taake point bilkul sahi jagah lage)
\[x = 2\cos 75^{\circ}\]
\[x \approx 2(0.2588) \approx 0.52\]
\[y = 2\sin 75^{\circ}\]
\[y \approx 2(0.9659) \approx 1.93\]
Kyun: \(x = r\cos\theta\) aur \(y = r\sin\theta\) wohi point x aur y ki zubaan mein de dete hain. Graph paper par x aur y se point lagana zyada pakka hota hai, aur is se quadrant bhi confirm ho jata hai: pehla (first) quadrant. Dono x aur y positive hain, jo first quadrant ki pehchaan hai. \(\cos 75^{\circ}\) aur \(\sin 75^{\circ}\) standard angles nahi, is liye calculator ki values li hain.

Point plot karein
O se \(75^{\circ}\) par ray kheenchein (protractor polar axis par rakh kar angle naapein), phir is ray par O se 2 units door point lagayein. Yeh point taqreeban \((0.52,\ 1.93)\) par aayega.
Kyun: polar coordinates mein angle direction batata hai aur \(|r|\) O se faasla. Polar grid ke circles (rings) faasla naapne mein madad dete hain: point ko us ring par lagayein jis ka radius \(|r|\) hai.

Tasdeeq (check):
Ab khud se poochiye: kya hamara point O se theek \(|r|\) faasle par hai? Pythagoras se faasle ka square \(x^{2} + y^{2}\) hota hai:
\[0.52^{2} + 1.93^{2} \approx 3.99 \approx 4\]
aur yeh \(2^{2} = 4\) ke barabar hai, yani point sahi jagah hai. (Chhota sa farq sirf decimal rounding ki wajah se hai.)
blocks.final_answer: Point \(75^{\circ}\) wali ray par, O se 2 units door, pehle (first) quadrant mein, taqreeban \((0.52,\ 1.93)\) par hai. Matlab: polar axis se \(75^{\circ}\) anticlockwise ghoom kar 2 qadam aage.

answer_figure.caption: Question 1 (i): the point plotted on a polar grid (original drawing)

blocks.explanation: Yeh sawal polar coordinates ka hai: humein ek point plot karna hai. Polar point \((r, \theta)\) mein \(\theta\) direction batata hai aur \(|r|\) origin O se faasla. Is part ki khaas baat yeh hai ke r negative hai. Negative r ka matlab hai: angle ki taraf munh kar ke ulte qadam chalna, yani O se guzar kar bilkul ulti taraf pohanchna. Bohat se students yahan point ko angle wali ray par hi laga dete hain, jo ghalat hai. Plan: angle ko degrees mein samjhein, negative r ki wajah se direction mein \(180^{\circ}\) jama karein, x aur y nikaalein, point lagayein aur faasla check karein.
steps:
Given (diya gaya hai): polar point \((-3,\ 120^{\circ})\), yani \(r = -3\) aur \(\theta = 120^{\circ}\).
To find (maloom karna hai): yeh point polar plane par kahan aata hai, aur use plot karna.
Method (tareeqa): pehle polar axis (yani positive x-axis) se angle \(\theta\) jitna ghoomein: \(\theta\) positive ho to anticlockwise (ghari ki suiyon ke ulat), negative ho to clockwise (ghari ki suiyon ki taraf). Phir us ray (seedhi lakeer jo O se shuru ho kar ek taraf jaati hai) par \(|r|\) units chalein. Agar \(r\) negative ho to isi ray ki bajaye ulti (opposite) ray par chalein.

Negative r ko handle karein
Yahan \(r\) negative hai. Is ka matlab hai ke angle wali ray ki taraf munh kar ke hum ulte qadam chalenge, yani O se guzar kar bilkul ulti taraf. Ulti taraf ka matlab direction mein \(180^{\circ}\) jama karna:
\[120^{\circ} + 180^{\circ} = 300^{\circ}\]
\[(-3,\ 120^{\circ}) = (3,\ 300^{\circ})\]
Kyun: \((-r, \theta)\) aur \((r, \theta + 180^{\circ})\) ek hi point ke do naam hain. Socho aap kisi darwaze ki taraf munh kar ke khare hain aur 3 qadam peeche hat-te hain: aap darwaze se ulti taraf pohanch jaate hain. Is tarah given angle \(120^{\circ}\) ki bajaye asal direction \(300^{\circ}\) ban jaati hai, aur ab faasla positive \(|r|\) hai. \(120^{\circ}\) second quadrant mein hai, is liye ulti taraf fourth quadrant mein pohanchte hain.
Dhyan dein: \(180^{\circ}\) jama karna hai, sirf angle ka sign badalna nahi. Angle ka sign badalne se point x-axis ke mirror mein chala jata hai, jo bilkul alag point hai.

Rectangular coordinates nikaalein (taake point bilkul sahi jagah lage)
\[x = -3\cos 120^{\circ}\]
\[x = -3\left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\right) = \dfrac{3}{2}\]
\[y = -3\sin 120^{\circ}\]
\[y = -3\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) \approx -2.60\]
Kyun: \(x = r\cos\theta\) aur \(y = r\sin\theta\) wohi point x aur y ki zubaan mein de dete hain. Graph paper par x aur y se point lagana zyada pakka hota hai, aur is se quadrant bhi confirm ho jata hai: chautha (fourth) quadrant. Yahan \(\cos 120^{\circ} = -\frac{1}{2}\) aur \(\sin 120^{\circ} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\) hain (standard angle, reference angle \(60^{\circ}\)); negative r se zarb dene par x positive aur y negative ho gaya.
Dhyan dein: yahan r ko us ke sign samet (jaisa diya hai) aur asal given angle ke saath istemal kiya hai; dono tareeqon (negative r ke saath given angle, ya positive \(|r|\) ke saath nayi direction) se bilkul wohi x aur y aate hain.

Point plot karein
O se \(300^{\circ}\) par ray kheenchein (protractor polar axis par rakh kar angle naapein), phir is ray par O se 3 units door point lagayein. Yeh point taqreeban \((1.5,\ -2.60)\) par aayega.
Kyun: polar coordinates mein angle direction batata hai aur \(|r|\) O se faasla. Polar grid ke circles (rings) faasla naapne mein madad dete hain: point ko us ring par lagayein jis ka radius \(|r|\) hai.

Tasdeeq (check):
Ab khud se poochiye: kya hamara point O se theek \(|r|\) faasle par hai? Pythagoras se faasle ka square \(x^{2} + y^{2}\) hota hai:
\[1.5^{2} + 2.60^{2} \approx 9.01 \approx 9\]
aur yeh \(3^{2} = 9\) ke barabar hai, yani point sahi jagah hai. (Chhota sa farq sirf decimal rounding ki wajah se hai.)
blocks.final_answer: Point \(300^{\circ}\) wali ray par, O se 3 units door, chauthay (fourth) quadrant mein, taqreeban \((1.5,\ -2.60)\) par hai; yeh wohi point hai jo \((3,\ 300^{\circ})\). Yani \(120^{\circ}\) ki taraf munh kar ke 3 qadam peeche.

Given (diya gaya hai): polar point \(\left(2,\ \frac{\pi}{6}\right)\), yani \(r = 2\) aur \(\theta = \frac{\pi}{6}\).

Angle ko degrees mein badlein
\[\dfrac{\pi}{6} = \dfrac{180^{\circ}}{6} = 30^{\circ}\]
Kyun: humein yaad hai ke \(\pi\) radian \(= 180^{\circ}\). Radian mein angle zehan mein tasveer nahi banata, lekin degrees mein foran andaza ho jata hai ke ray kis taraf hai. Yahan \(\frac{\pi}{6}\) ka matlab hai \(180^{\circ}\) ka chhata hissa, yani \(30^{\circ}\).

r ka sign dekhein
\(r = 2 > 0\), is liye point isi \(30^{\circ}\) wali ray par hoga.
Kyun: positive r ka matlab hai ray ke saath aage chalna; direction nahi badalti. \(30^{\circ}\) first quadrant mein hai, polar axis ke qareeb.

Rectangular coordinates nikaalein (taake point bilkul sahi jagah lage)
\[x = 2\cos 30^{\circ} = 2 \cdot \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\]
\[x = \sqrt{3} \approx 1.73\]
\[y = 2\sin 30^{\circ} = 2 \cdot \dfrac{1}{2} = 1\]
Kyun: \(x = r\cos\theta\) aur \(y = r\sin\theta\) wohi point x aur y ki zubaan mein de dete hain. Graph paper par x aur y se point lagana zyada pakka hota hai, aur is se quadrant bhi confirm ho jata hai: pehla (first) quadrant. \(30^{\circ}\) standard angle hai: \(\cos 30^{\circ} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\), \(\sin 30^{\circ} = \frac{1}{2}\). Is liye yahan exact values mil gayin, calculator ki zaroorat nahi.

Point plot karein
O se \(30^{\circ}\) par ray kheenchein (protractor polar axis par rakh kar angle naapein), phir is ray par O se 2 units door point lagayein. Yeh point taqreeban \((1.73,\ 1)\) par aayega.
Kyun: polar coordinates mein angle direction batata hai aur \(|r|\) O se faasla. Polar grid ke circles (rings) faasla naapne mein madad dete hain: point ko us ring par lagayein jis ka radius \(|r|\) hai.

Tasdeeq (check):
Ab khud se poochiye: kya hamara point O se theek \(|r|\) faasle par hai? Pythagoras se faasle ka square \(x^{2} + y^{2}\) hota hai:
\[(\sqrt{3})^{2} + 1^{2} = 3 + 1 = 4\]
aur yeh \(2^{2} = 4\) ke barabar hai, yani point sahi jagah hai. (Chhota sa farq sirf decimal rounding ki wajah se hai.)
blocks.final_answer: Point \(30^{\circ}\) wali ray par, O se 2 units door, pehle (first) quadrant mein, taqreeban \((1.73,\ 1)\) par hai.

Point plot karein
O se \(150^{\circ}\) par ray kheenchein (protractor polar axis par rakh kar angle naapein), phir is ray par O se 5 units door point lagayein. Yeh point taqreeban \((-4.33,\ 2.5)\) par aayega.

blocks.final_answer: Point \(150^{\circ}\) wali ray par, O se 5 units door, doosre (second) quadrant mein, taqreeban \((-4.33,\ 2.5)\) par hai. Yeh grid ke sab se bahar wale (5 wale) ring par aata hai.

steps:
Given (diya gaya hai): polar point \(\left(-\frac{5}{2},\ \frac{\pi}{3}\right)\), yani \(r = -\frac{5}{2}\) aur \(\theta = \frac{\pi}{3}\).
To find (maloom karna hai): yeh point polar plane par kahan aata hai, aur use plot karna.
Method (tareeqa): pehle polar axis (yani positive x-axis) se angle \(\theta\) jitna ghoomein: \(\theta\) positive ho to anticlockwise (ghari ki suiyon ke ulat), negative ho to clockwise (ghari ki suiyon ki taraf). \[\dfrac{\pi}{3} = \dfrac{180^{\circ}}{3} = 60^{\circ}\]
Kyun: humein yaad hai ke \(\pi\) radian \(= 180^{\circ}\). Radian mein angle zehan mein tasveer nahi banata, lekin degrees mein foran andaza ho jata hai ke ray kis taraf hai. \(\frac{\pi}{3}\) yani \(180^{\circ}\) ka teesra hissa, \(60^{\circ}\).

\[60^{\circ} + 180^{\circ} = 240^{\circ}\]
\[\left(-\frac{5}{2},\ \frac{\pi}{3}\right) = \left(\frac{5}{2},\ 240^{\circ}\right)\]
Kyun: \((-r, \theta)\) aur \((r, \theta + 180^{\circ})\) ek hi point ke do naam hain. Socho aap kisi darwaze ki taraf munh kar ke khare hain aur 3 qadam peeche hat-te hain: aap darwaze se ulti taraf pohanch jaate hain. Is tarah given angle \(60^{\circ}\) ki bajaye asal direction \(240^{\circ}\) ban jaati hai, aur ab faasla positive \(|r|\) hai. \(60^{\circ}\) first quadrant mein hai, to ulti taraf third quadrant mein aate hain.
Dhyan dein: \(180^{\circ}\) jama karna hai, sirf angle ka sign badalna nahi. Angle ka sign badalne se point x-axis ke mirror mein chala jata hai, jo bilkul alag point hai.

Rectangular coordinates nikaalein (taake point bilkul sahi jagah lage)
\[x = -\dfrac{5}{2}\cos 60^{\circ} = -\dfrac{5}{2} \cdot \dfrac{1}{2}\]
\[x = -\dfrac{5}{4} = -1.25\]
\[y = -\dfrac{5}{2}\sin 60^{\circ} = -\dfrac{5\sqrt{3}}{4}\]
\[y \approx -2.17\]
Kyun: \(x = r\cos\theta\) aur \(y = r\sin\theta\) wohi point x aur y ki zubaan mein de dete hain. Graph paper par x aur y se point lagana zyada pakka hota hai, aur is se quadrant bhi confirm ho jata hai: teesra (third) quadrant. \(\cos 60^{\circ} = \frac{1}{2}\) aur \(\sin 60^{\circ} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\) dono positive hain, lekin negative r se zarb dene par dono x aur y negative ho gaye, jo third quadrant ki nishani hai.
Dhyan dein: yahan r ko us ke sign samet (jaisa diya hai) aur asal given angle ke saath istemal kiya hai; dono tareeqon (negative r ke saath given angle, ya positive \(|r|\) ke saath nayi direction) se bilkul wohi x aur y aate hain.

Point plot karein
O se \(240^{\circ}\) par ray kheenchein (protractor polar axis par rakh kar angle naapein), phir is ray par O se 2.5 units door point lagayein. Yeh point taqreeban \((-1.25,\ -2.17)\) par aayega.
Kyun: polar coordinates mein angle direction batata hai aur \(|r|\) O se faasla. Polar grid ke circles (rings) faasla naapne mein madad dete hain: point ko us ring par lagayein jis ka radius \(|r|\) hai.

Ab khud se poochiye: kya hamara point O se theek \(|r|\) faasle par hai? Pythagoras se faasle ka square \(x^{2} + y^{2}\) hota hai:
\[\dfrac{25}{16} + \dfrac{75}{16} = \dfrac{100}{16} = 6.25\]
aur yeh \((5/2)^{2} = 6.25\) ke barabar hai, yani point sahi jagah hai. (Chhota sa farq sirf decimal rounding ki wajah se hai.)

Is tarah given angle \(-120^{\circ}\) ki bajaye asal direction \(60^{\circ}\) ban jaati hai, aur ab faasla positive \(|r|\) hai. Third quadrant ki ulti taraf first quadrant hai. Dekhiye, yahan do minus (angle ka aur r ka) mil kar point ko first quadrant mein le aaye.
Dhyan dein: \(180^{\circ}\) jama karna hai, sirf angle ka sign badalna nahi. Angle ka sign badalne se point x-axis ke mirror mein chala jata hai, jo bilkul alag point hai.

Rectangular coordinates nikaalein (taake point bilkul sahi jagah lage)
\[x = -3\cos(-120^{\circ}) = -3\left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\right)\]
\[x = \dfrac{3}{2} = 1.5\]
\[y = -3\sin(-120^{\circ}) = -3\left(-\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)\]
\[y = \dfrac{3\sqrt{3}}{2} \approx 2.60\]
Kyun: \(x = r\cos\theta\) aur \(y = r\sin\theta\) wohi point x aur y ki zubaan mein de dete hain. Graph paper par x aur y se point lagana zyada pakka hota hai, aur is se quadrant bhi confirm ho jata hai: pehla (first) quadrant. Yahan \(\cos(-120^{\circ}) = -\frac{1}{2}\) aur \(\sin(-120^{\circ}) = -\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\) dono negative hain; negative r se zarb dene par dono positive ho gaye.
Dhyan dein: yahan r ko us ke sign samet (jaisa diya hai) aur asal given angle ke saath istemal kiya hai; dono tareeqon (negative r ke saath given angle, ya positive \(|r|\) ke saath nayi direction) se bilkul wohi x aur y aate hain.

Point plot karein
O se \(60^{\circ}\) par ray kheenchein (protractor polar axis par rakh kar angle naapein), phir is ray par O se 3 units door point lagayein. Yeh point taqreeban \((1.5,\ 2.60)\) par aayega.
Kyun: polar coordinates mein angle direction batata hai aur \(|r|\) O se faasla. Polar grid ke circles (rings) faasla naapne mein madad dete hain: point ko us ring par lagayein jis ka radius \(|r|\) hai.

Tasdeeq (check):
Ab khud se poochiye: kya hamara point O se theek \(|r|\) faasle par hai? Pythagoras se faasle ka square \(x^{2} + y^{2}\) hota hai:
\[\dfrac{9}{4} + \dfrac{27}{4} = \dfrac{36}{4} = 9\]
aur yeh \(3^{2} = 9\) ke barabar hai, yani point sahi jagah hai. (Chhota sa farq sirf decimal rounding ki wajah se hai.)
blocks.final_answer: Point \(60^{\circ}\) wali ray par, O se 3 units door, pehle (first) quadrant mein, taqreeban \((1.5,\ 2.60)\) par hai; yeh wohi point hai jo \((3,\ 60^{\circ})\).

blocks.explanation: Yeh sawal polar coordinates ka hai: humein ek point plot karna hai. Polar point \((r, \theta)\) mein \(\theta\) direction batata hai aur \(|r|\) origin O se faasla. Is part ki khaas baat yeh hai ke r negative hai. Negative r ka matlab hai: angle ki taraf munh kar ke ulte qadam chalna, yani O se guzar kar bilkul ulti taraf pohanchna. Bohat se students yahan point ko angle wali ray par hi laga dete hain, jo ghalat hai. Plan: angle ko degrees mein samjhein, negative r ki wajah se direction mein \(180^{\circ}\) jama karein, x aur y nikaalein, point lagayein aur faasla check karein. Angle bhi bara aur negative hai, is liye pehle use ek aasaan angle mein badlenge. (Kitab ne is part ko ghalti se dobara (iii) likha hai; hum ise (vii) kehte hain.)
steps:
Given (diya gaya hai): polar point \(\left(-\frac{9}{2},\ -\frac{19\pi}{12}\right)\), yani \(r = -\frac{9}{2}\) aur \(\theta = -\frac{19\pi}{12}\).
To find (maloom karna hai): yeh point polar plane par kahan aata hai, aur use plot karna.
Method (tareeqa): pehle polar axis (yani positive x-axis) se angle \(\theta\) jitna ghoomein: \(\theta\) positive ho to anticlockwise (ghari ki suiyon ke ulat), negative ho to clockwise (ghari ki suiyon ki taraf). Phir us ray (seedhi lakeer jo O se shuru ho kar ek taraf jaati hai) par \(|r|\) units chalein. Agar \(r\) negative ho to isi ray ki bajaye ulti (opposite) ray par chalein.

Angle ko degrees mein badlein aur aasaan banayein
\[\dfrac{\pi}{12} = 15^{\circ}\]
\[-\dfrac{19\pi}{12} = -19 \times 15^{\circ} = -285^{\circ}\]
\[-285^{\circ} + 360^{\circ} = 75^{\circ}\]
Kyun: \(\pi\) radian \(= 180^{\circ}\), is liye \(\frac{\pi}{12} = 15^{\circ}\). \(-285^{\circ}\) ka matlab hai \(285^{\circ}\) clockwise ghoomna. Poora chakkar (\(360^{\circ}\)) jama karne se direction nahi badalti, sirf angle aasaan ho jata hai: \(-285^{\circ}\) aur \(75^{\circ}\) ek hi ray hain.
Dhyan dein: \(360^{\circ}\) jama ya minus karna hamesha jaiz hai, kyunke ek poora chakkar laga kar hum wahin wapas aa jaate hain.

Negative r ko handle karein
Yahan \(r\) negative hai. Is ka matlab hai ke angle wali ray ki taraf munh kar ke hum ulte qadam chalenge, yani O se guzar kar bilkul ulti taraf. Ulti taraf ka matlab direction mein \(180^{\circ}\) jama karna:
\[75^{\circ} + 180^{\circ} = 255^{\circ}\]
\[\left(-\frac{9}{2},\ -\frac{19\pi}{12}\right) = \left(\frac{9}{2},\ 255^{\circ}\right)\]
Kyun: \((-r, \theta)\) aur \((r, \theta + 180^{\circ})\) ek hi point ke do naam hain. Socho aap kisi darwaze ki taraf munh kar ke khare hain aur 3 qadam peeche hat-te hain: aap darwaze se ulti taraf pohanch jaate hain. Is tarah given angle \(75^{\circ}\) ki bajaye asal direction \(255^{\circ}\) ban jaati hai, aur ab faasla positive \(|r|\) hai. \(75^{\circ}\) first quadrant mein hai, is ki ulti taraf third quadrant hai.
Dhyan dein: \(180^{\circ}\) jama karna hai, sirf angle ka sign badalna nahi. Angle ka sign badalne se point x-axis ke mirror mein chala jata hai, jo bilkul alag point hai.

Rectangular coordinates nikaalein (taake point bilkul sahi jagah lage)
\[x = -\dfrac{9}{2}\cos 75^{\circ}\]
\[x \approx -4.5(0.2588) \approx -1.16\]
\[y = -\dfrac{9}{2}\sin 75^{\circ}\]
\[y \approx -4.5(0.9659) \approx -4.35\]
Kyun: \(x = r\cos\theta\) aur \(y = r\sin\theta\) wohi point x aur y ki zubaan mein de dete hain. Graph paper par x aur y se point lagana zyada pakka hota hai, aur is se quadrant bhi confirm ho jata hai: teesra (third) quadrant. Hum ne \(\theta\) ki jagah aasaan angle \(75^{\circ}\) istemal kiya (cos aur sin poore chakkar se nahi badalte). Negative r ki wajah se dono x aur y negative aaye.
Dhyan dein: yahan r ko us ke sign samet (jaisa diya hai) aur asal given angle ke saath istemal kiya hai; dono tareeqon (negative r ke saath given angle, ya positive \(|r|\) ke saath nayi direction) se bilkul wohi x aur y aate hain.

Point plot karein
O se \(255^{\circ}\) par ray kheenchein (protractor polar axis par rakh kar angle naapein), phir is ray par O se 4.5 units door point lagayein. Yeh point taqreeban \((-1.16,\ -4.35)\) par aayega.
Kyun: polar coordinates mein angle direction batata hai aur \(|r|\) O se faasla. Polar grid ke circles (rings) faasla naapne mein madad dete hain: point ko us ring par lagayein jis ka radius \(|r|\) hai.

Tasdeeq (check):
Ab khud se poochiye: kya hamara point O se theek \(|r|\) faasle par hai? Pythagoras se faasle ka square \(x^{2} + y^{2}\) hota hai:
\[1.16^{2} + 4.35^{2} \approx 20.27 \approx 20.25\]
aur yeh \(4.5^{2} = 20.25\) ke barabar hai, yani point sahi jagah hai. (Chhota sa farq sirf decimal rounding ki wajah se hai.)
blocks.final_answer: Point \(255^{\circ}\) wali ray par, O se 4.5 units door, teesre (third) quadrant mein, taqreeban \((-1.16,\ -4.35)\) par hai; yeh wohi point hai jo \(\left(\frac{9}{2},\ 255^{\circ}\right)\).

Bohat se students yahan point ko angle wali ray par hi laga dete hain, jo ghalat hai. (Kitab ne is part ko ghalti se dobara (iv) likha hai; hum ise (viii) kehte hain. Is ki answer key ki drawing bhi ghalat hai, neeche correction dekhiye.)
steps:
Given (diya gaya hai): polar point \(\left(-\frac{5}{2},\ \frac{5\pi}{12}\right)\), yani \(r = -\frac{5}{2}\) aur \(\theta = \frac{5\pi}{12}\).
To find (maloom karna hai): yeh point polar plane par kahan aata hai, aur use plot karna.
Method (tareeqa): pehle polar axis (yani positive x-axis) se angle \(\theta\) jitna ghoomein: \(\theta\) positive ho to anticlockwise (ghari ki suiyon ke ulat), negative ho to clockwise (ghari ki suiyon ki taraf). Phir us ray (seedhi lakeer jo O se shuru ho kar ek taraf jaati hai) par \(|r|\) units chalein. Agar \(r\) negative ho to isi ray ki bajaye ulti (opposite) ray par chalein.

Angle ko degrees mein badlein
\[\dfrac{5\pi}{12} = 5 \times 15^{\circ} = 75^{\circ}\]
Kyun: humein yaad hai ke \(\pi\) radian \(= 180^{\circ}\). Radian mein angle zehan mein tasveer nahi banata, lekin degrees mein foran andaza ho jata hai ke ray kis taraf hai. \(\frac{\pi}{12} = 15^{\circ}\), to \(\frac{5\pi}{12}\) us ka paanch guna, \(75^{\circ}\).

Negative r ko handle karein
Yahan \(r\) negative hai. Is ka matlab hai ke angle wali ray ki taraf munh kar ke hum ulte qadam chalenge, yani O se guzar kar bilkul ulti taraf. Ulti taraf ka matlab direction mein \(180^{\circ}\) jama karna:
\[75^{\circ} + 180^{\circ} = 255^{\circ}\]
\[\left(-\frac{5}{2},\ \frac{5\pi}{12}\right) = \left(\frac{5}{2},\ 255^{\circ}\right)\]
Kyun: \((-r, \theta)\) aur \((r, \theta + 180^{\circ})\) ek hi point ke do naam hain. Socho aap kisi darwaze ki taraf munh kar ke khare hain aur 3 qadam peeche hat-te hain: aap darwaze se ulti taraf pohanch jaate hain. Is tarah given angle \(75^{\circ}\) ki bajaye asal direction \(255^{\circ}\) ban jaati hai, aur ab faasla positive \(|r|\) hai. Yahi woh jagah hai jahan answer key ne ghalti ki: us ne point ko second quadrant mein dikhaya, jab ke ulti taraf third quadrant hai.
Dhyan dein: \(180^{\circ}\) jama karna hai, sirf angle ka sign badalna nahi. Angle ka sign badalne se point x-axis ke mirror mein chala jata hai, jo bilkul alag point hai.

Rectangular coordinates nikaalein (taake point bilkul sahi jagah lage)
\[x = -\dfrac{5}{2}\cos 75^{\circ}\]
\[x \approx -2.5(0.2588) \approx -0.65\]
\[y = -\dfrac{5}{2}\sin 75^{\circ}\]
\[y \approx -2.5(0.9659) \approx -2.41\]
Kyun: \(x = r\cos\theta\) aur \(y = r\sin\theta\) wohi point x aur y ki zubaan mein de dete hain. Graph paper par x aur y se point lagana zyada pakka hota hai, aur is se quadrant bhi confirm ho jata hai: teesra (third) quadrant. Dono x aur y negative hain, yani point O se neeche aur baayein hai. Yeh pichle part (vii) wali ray par hi hai, bas O ke zyada qareeb (4.5 ki jagah 2.5).
Dhyan dein: yahan r ko us ke sign samet (jaisa diya hai) aur asal given angle ke saath istemal kiya hai; dono tareeqon (negative r ke saath given angle, ya positive \(|r|\) ke saath nayi direction) se bilkul wohi x aur y aate hain.

Point plot karein
O se \(255^{\circ}\) par ray kheenchein (protractor polar axis par rakh kar angle naapein), phir is ray par O se 2.5 units door point lagayein. Yeh point taqreeban \((-0.65,\ -2.41)\) par aayega.
Kyun: polar coordinates mein angle direction batata hai aur \(|r|\) O se faasla. Polar grid ke circles (rings) faasla naapne mein madad dete hain: point ko us ring par lagayein jis ka radius \(|r|\) hai.

Tasdeeq (check):
Ab khud se poochiye: kya hamara point O se theek \(|r|\) faasle par hai? Pythagoras se faasle ka square \(x^{2} + y^{2}\) hota hai:
\[0.65^{2} + 2.41^{2} \approx 6.23 \approx 6.25\]
aur yeh \(2.5^{2} = 6.25\) ke barabar hai, yani point sahi jagah hai. (Chhota sa farq sirf decimal rounding ki wajah se hai.)
blocks.final_answer: Point \(255^{\circ}\) wali ray par, O se 2.5 units door, teesre (third) quadrant mein, taqreeban \((-0.65,\ -2.41)\) par hai; yeh wohi point hai jo \(\left(\frac{5}{2},\ 255^{\circ}\right)\).

blocks.text: Answer key ki drawing 1 (viii) (jo kitab mein doosri baar (iv) likha hai) mein point ko second quadrant mein, O se upar aur baayein, dikhati hai. Lekin \(r = -\frac{5}{2}\) negative hai, is liye point \(75^{\circ} + 180^{\circ} = 255^{\circ}\) wali ray par, third quadrant mein, taqreeban \((-0.65, -2.41)\) par hai.
